key_insight: ReproBridge explores whether preserving recovered experimental procedures and decisions can make independent ML reproduction more reliable. The central idea is to build reproducibility into research artifacts rather than rely on coding agents to infer missing details.
problem_solved: Experimental instructions are scattered across papers, code, and supporting materials, making reproduction depend on an agent’s ability to reconstruct undocumented steps.
method: Define a standardized research artifact design that includes a refined codebase and environment information.
Preserve procedures and decisions recovered while reconstructing experiments.
Investigate whether these enriched artifacts improve subsequent independent reproduction; the provided abstract is incomplete and reports no results.
impact: More explicit research artifacts could reduce repeated investigative work and make ML experiments easier to reproduce. This would help practitioners distinguish artifact quality from a coding agent’s ability to fill information gaps.
visual_elements: Before-and-after diagram: scattered paper, code, and supporting files → standardized artifact.
Workflow: reconstruct experiment → preserve procedures and decisions → independent reproduction.
Artifact checklist with icons for code, environment, procedures, and decisions.
Contrast graphic: agent-inferred instructions versus explicitly documented steps.
paper_title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
paper_authors: Yubo Wang, Rui Meng, Jaehyun Nam, Tomas Pfister, Jinsung Yoon
